[curious, lively, starts speaking immediately] Paid for something that never arrived? Federal law gives you a way to fight it, and plenty of people never use it. The Fair Credit Billing Act lets you dispute credit card errors, including things you paid for but never got. But the clock is ticking. You generally have sixty days from that statement to send your dispute to the card issuer. While the card issuer investigates, you generally do not have to pay the disputed amount or the interest on it. Keep receipts, emails, and tracking numbers, because clear evidence is what wins disputes. Paid for something that never came? Fight it.
